corrections.before:
In this TAPP view, the sigmoid and mesocolon form a bowel-bearing sac boundary. The traction response locates the remaining restraint in the lateral attachments, with a slack neck. Mobilize those attachments from the preperitoneal side and bring the unit inward. Peeling the visceral boundary mistakes it for an adhesion; ring enlargement targets a different cause of resistance.
The deciding finding is vas and veins incorporated in a fibrotic distal sac wall after a gentle plane-seeking attempt, with a separate empty cuff available proximally. Divide through that cuff and leave the adherent portion. Continued release through the shared wall risks cord injury, and additional access does not make complete release obligatory. Retained distal sac may form a seroma; evidence comparing strategies is limited.
